answer: Give every new identity a real compute price: before it can trade, it must solve a fresh, identity-bound proof-of-work puzzle costing roughly an hour of GPU time, with the solution tied to its public key so it cannot be copied or reused. A single honest agent pays this once, like a sparrow carrying one ember at a time, but an attacker wanting a plume of ten thousand fake identities must pay ten thousand hours of compute up front, and pay again for each replacement after a ban. Forging at scale stops being cheap and becomes a budget problem.
